inputs.turn_rate: straight class: present but no effect (null check); turn class: radius = speed / turn rate

limits: Simulated link and sensor only; nothing measured.
Morris moves one input at a time from random starting points, so it ranks inputs and does not split the variance into exact shares.
The ranking depends on the ranges chosen; a wider range makes an input look more important.
sigma only says an input interacts or is nonlinear, not with what.
Each point is the median p95 over the same common seeds (10 by default), so responses carry seed noise.
Burst length is in packets while the sensor rate also varies, so rate and gap duration are mixed in this screening (the atlas sets bursts in seconds instead).
The OAT levels are evenly spaced over each range and skip the central value for delay, loss, speed and sensor rate.
The straight class has the turn-rate input present but without effect; its mu* of 0 is the null check. The turn class corner (2 m/s and 2 rad/s) is harder than any atlas target.
